# Methodology Document — Skeleton

**Status:** To be completed after master report is finalized.

This document provides detailed methodology for the AI-assisted survey harmonization research. All source material is in `archive/research_notes/` (former Reports 01–03).

## Planned Sections

### 1. Data Preparation

- Survey instrument collection and digitization
- Question deduplication (7,419 raw → 6,987 deduplicated)
- Survey instrument inventory (47 instruments across ~30 programs)

### 2. Classification Framework

- Census topic/subtopic taxonomy design
- Dual-model classification protocol (GPT-5-mini, Claude Haiku 4.5)
- Consensus resolution for classification disagreements
- Confidence scoring

### 3. Survey Overlap Analysis

- Concept overlap computation methodology
- ACS anchor selection rationale
- Survey family identification algorithm
- Pair selection criteria

### 4. Barrier Taxonomy

- Taxonomy development process
- Six barrier categories with sub-codes
- Three feasibility tiers
- Prompt engineering for consistent barrier application

### 5. Multi-Model Rating Protocol

- Three-rater independent assessment design
- Model selection rationale (vendor diversity, capability tier)
- Temperature and parameter settings (from `config/report_03.yaml`)
- Rate limiting and checkpoint/resume architecture

### 6. Arbitration Protocol

- Disagreement detection and routing
- Arbitrator model selection (higher capability tier)
- Arbitration prompt design
- Verdict aggregation rules

### 7. Question-Level Rollup

- Pair-to-question collapse logic
- Two-axis triage scoring (Borda direction × Entropy stability)
- Expert review routing criteria
- Quality gate definitions

### 8. Statistical Framework

- Cohen's kappa and Fleiss' kappa interpretation
- The kappa paradox in skewed distributions
- Agreement stratification (by survey, topic, barrier)
- Statistical power considerations

### 9. Reproducibility

- Pipeline architecture (5 stages, JSON intermediate files)
- Configuration-driven model parameters
- Checkpoint/resume for API reliability
- Public code and data repository
